state:
Goal `core-session`, stage 2. `Core\Session::clear`, `destroy` and `get` have all their feature proofs: about, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure, a Rust `covers:` test and a card in the plain voice. `Core\Session` has a class card. Six members still owe examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` test: `start`, `set`, `remove`, `regenerate`, `setSecret`, `getSecret`.

Every Session proof needs a real store and a real request. The shape is on disk under `docs/examples/core/Session/clear/`: an `nvs.toml` in the feature directory that grants `[capabilities.cache] shared`, sets `[session] backend = "shared"` and `[cache.shared] url = "redis://127.0.0.1:16379"`, and a `.nvsr` beside each program. `tests/hostile/core/Session/<member>/` has the same pair. `benches/members/core/Session/nvs.toml` already serves every Session bench, so a new bench needs only its own `.nvs` and `.nvsr`. Redis is `tests/db/compose.yaml`'s service, which the goal's `env.docker` brings up.

A member that talks to the store can still be tested from Rust through the real member: `destroy_forgets_the_record_before_it_closes_the_session` sets `crate::tests::granting` with a `[cache.shared] url` pointing at the loopback `serving` fake, and `open_configured` dials it. A member that talks to the store costs a round trip per call on this host (about 0.7 ms), so its bench uses a few thousand iterations, not a hundred thousand.

A bench's figure goes stale whenever `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs` changes. After the last Rust edit, run `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Session'` and `--record-perf --id '<member>'` for each member it names stale.

next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs`, the proof trees under `core/Session/`.

items.text: **`Core\Session::remove`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:380` and the member `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1249`. Rewrite the card in the plain voice, as `GET_DOC` now is. A Rust test through `nvs_runtime::call` needs no store, as `get_answers_a_held_key_and_null_for_the_rest_and_earns_no_write` shows; assert that removing a key the record does not hold earns no write.

**`Core\Session::set`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests. The card is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:342`, the member `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1152`. The attack should try a value the cross-boundary copy refuses (a closure, deep nesting), which throws `LogicError`.

**`Core\Session::setSecret` and `getSecret`** — owe the same. The cards are `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:468` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:513`, the members `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1193` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1225`. `session_secret_is_stored_as_ciphertext_in_the_record` exists and may take a `covers:` marker for both if it calls both members; read it first.

backlog: `Core\Session::start` and `regenerate` owe the same proofs, and both reach the store; drive them over `serving` as the `destroy` test does (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs`).

`Core\Session::get` decodes the whole record on every call (13 allocations for a three-key record in its bench); a cached decode is a perf question for `rule:http-server/a-session-is-loaded-once-and-written-whole`, not a proof gap.
